content.text: Innerworks and HumbleBeeAI: Building Fraud-Defense Infrastructure Through R&D Partnership
HumbleBeeAI partnered with Innerworks from January 2024 as its R&D and product arm to develop modular fraud-defense capabilities for exchanges, finance platforms and digital ecosystems.

attrs.chunkText: Innerworks is a cybersecurity / behavioral intelligence company focused on helping exchanges, finance platforms, and digital ecosystems identify and block bad actors. Their solution stack includes Account Takeover Protection, Geo Compliance, Bot detection, and deeper behavioral analysis, leveraging 200+ data points across device, network, and behavioral signals. They also employ a RedTeam ethical hacking platform (built on BitTensor) to stay ahead of AI-driven fraud techniques. Starting in January 2024, HumbleBeeAI partnered with Innerworks as their R&D and product arm, building the core infrastructure and capabilities that enabled them to secure a $4M seed round in August 2025 led by AlbionVC.

content.text: Executive Summary

Innerworks helps digital platforms identify and block bad actors, but when the partnership began it had a foundational SDK rather than a fully integrated solution—and lacked dedicated R&D capacity, senior fraud-and-AI engineering leadership and the infrastructure to grow its modules into a scalable platform. HumbleBeeAI joined in January 2024 to research, design, prototype and build capabilities alongside Innerworks’ teams. The company update reports that Innerworks raised a $4M seed round led by AlbionVC in August 2025; this is a reported company milestone, not a measured attribution of business impact to any individual capability.

From Collaboration to Innovation: Inside the Innerworks and HumbleBeeAI Partnership
Context and Challenge

Innerworks serves exchanges, finance platforms and digital ecosystems that need to detect account takeover, bots, suspicious locations and other signs of abuse. At the start of the engagement in January 2024, its single SDK provided a foundation for detection and fingerprinting, but the company lacked a dedicated R&D team, senior engineering leadership in fraud and AI, and infrastructure to integrate its modules into a cohesive platform.

content.text: Solution and Capabilities

Innerworks defined the product vision and goals; HumbleBeeAI acted as a collaborative R&D and product arm, researching, prototyping, iterating and building capabilities with Innerworks’ teams. The source describes modular architecture intended for R&D and collaboration on production integration, rather than claiming that every component was independently verified as deployed in production.

attrs.chunkText: We stepped in not as an outsourcing shop, but as their R&D & product arm. Innerworks defined the vision and product goals; our role was to design, research, prototype, iterate, and build those capabilities in collaboration with the other teams of Innerworks.

Deep domain research: industry best practices, academic papers, red-team methods, advanced heuristics.

Transparent knowledge transfer: all research, findings, designs, code, and docs are shared in their repositories, fully accessible. This ensures trust and enables seamless eventual transition or scaling by their team.

Successive iterations: we launched MVPs, collected feedback, adapted to adversarial behavior, and hardened models.

We structured the architecture of Device Fingerprinting, VPN / True Location Detection, Bot Detection / Behavioral Profiling, and RedTeam & Adversarial Testing Framework to be modular for research and development (R&D) purposes, while also supporting collaboration for production integration. Each component is designed to operate independently or feed into composite risk scoring flows. We have built pipelines for internal data ingestion, feature extraction, model serving, API endpoints, and monitoring, ensuring flexibility for both R&D experimentation and seamless production deployment through collaboration.

Throughout, we prioritized observability, scalability, reliability, and defensibility so that Innerworks could offer credible enterprise-grade services.

content.text: Modular fraud-defense capabilities

Device fingerprinting and device intelligence: developed as a module to contribute device-level signals to detection and risk analysis. Innerworks’ wider solution is described as leveraging 200+ data points across device, network and behavioral signals; the source does not specify that this is a count of device signals alone.

content.text: Results and Business Impact

The supplied company update reports product and financing milestones, but it provides no measured before-and-after fraud rate, detection accuracy, false-positive rate, latency, coverage improvement or financial return. The available outcomes should therefore be read as reported project status and company context—not as quantified business impact or a benchmark evaluation.

In August 2025, Innerworks raised $4M in a Seed round led by AlbionVC, demonstrating investor confidence in their technological foundation and trajectory.

They now maintain a stable client base across exchanges and digital platforms.

They use their full suite: device fingerprinting, VPN detection, bot detection, and threat intelligence – capabilities we co-built and matured.

Importantly, we ensured that all knowledge, research, code, documentation, and design artifacts remain in their repos (not ours). This fosters mutual trust and enables seamless handover or future scaling by their internal team.
